owner_signature_observed.meaning: a valid on-chain ECDSA signature from an AtomWallet owner is observable after an executed UserOp

high_s_counterpart_derivable.meaning: an observer can derive a high-s counterpart s' = curve_order - s, v' = v XOR 1 recovering the identical signer address

high_s_constructable_against_live_wallet.meaning: high-s signatures are technically valid ECDSA and a high-s counterpart of any valid owner signature is constructable against any live wallet

signature_mismatch_present.meaning: the UserOp signature presented to validateUserOp is a mismatch (the derived high-s counterpart rejected by tryRecover)

validation_failed_returned_without_rever.meaning: validateUserOp returns SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED (1) on the signature mismatch without reverting

griefing_repeatable.meaning: adversary can repeatedly submit griefing UserOps targeting any AtomWallet using the constructable high-s signature

assumptions: High-s signatures are technically valid ECDSA and a high-s counterpart of any valid owner signature is constructable against any live wallet.
The griefing UserOp is submitted to the EntryPoint handleOps path that calls validateUserOp without try/catch.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the griefing UserOp was actually observed on-chain; the impact is described as potential/conditional, so the repeatability relation is a potential outcome rather than an observed event.

limitations: Formalizes only the repeatable-griefing impact; bundler compute waste, batch gas loss, and wallet degradation are separate impacts not covered by this plan.
The repeatability relation is represented as a grounded Boolean because the report gives no numeric count or rate for repeated submissions.
The no-revert return obligation is encoded as a Boolean occurrence symbol because the report gives no numeric definition beyond the SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED (1) return value.
